subject: Private fleet pinning & safety protocol — staging/rollback review
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, acme-sre@acmehealth.com
Cc: ops-legal@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-09-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private fleet pinning & safety protocol — staging/rollback review

Hi all,

Following up from last week's ops sync: attached is a first-draft staging matrix for version pinning across the private fleet (staged_pin_matrix.xlsx). Key asks before we lock windows:

- Confirm the maintenance window for Acme Health (we propose Sat 09/18 02:00-06:00 PT).
- Agree on pinning semantics: we will pin 1) control-plane components, 2) runtime images (gRPC + runtime kernels), 3) model artifacts in S3 when applicable.
- Rollback criteria: CPU > 80% sustained for 10m, error rate spike > 3x baseline, or memory eviction on more than 5% of nodes.
- Network quarantine step: prior to pinning, cordon a small subset and run KV-cache integrity checks.

Please review the matrix and the short rollback checklist I attached. If Acme SRE has constraints that make staged pinning risky (network topology, HA pairs that can't be drained), flag them here.

Attachments: staged_pin_matrix.xlsx, rollback_checklist.md

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Sr. Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, acme-sre@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-09-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet pinning & safety protocol — staging/rollback review

Thanks Soojin — quick notes after skimming the matrix:

- Canary scope: propose we run canaries on the non-prod tenant pool first (5% of nodes), then a small cross-region canary of mixed traffic for 2 hours. If all green, proceed to 25% pin, then full.
- Network quarantine: add an explicit "egress-only" quarantine where we restrict outbound control-plane calls for a subset to detect latency regressions.
- KV cache verification: add a step to compare pre/post KV cache digests (sha256) — this will be in rollback_checklist.md.

Two asks for Acme: what are your expected RTOs for model-serving endpoints? We need that to calibrate our abort thresholds.

Attaching an early checklist excerpt for the rollback officer to own.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Manager, Release Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Acme SRE <acme-sre@acmehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-legal@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-09-03T07:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet pinning & safety protocol — staging/rollback review

Appreciate the draft. A few constraints from our side:

- We cannot accept a full fleet pin that requires a cross-datacenter restart during business hours. The window proposed is OK but the runbook must guarantee <5% traffic loss during staged steps.
- We need a signed snapshot of audit logs (pre/post) sent to our compliance inbox; SOC2 requires immutable evidence of the pre-change state. Can Redwood provide a read-only export and a hash digest?
- Topology note: our east-west fabric has active-active pairs with symmetric BGP; draining must respect affinity so we don't break sticky sessions.

We attached a short impact CSV from our last minor upgrade to illustrate node-level latencies (acme_patch_impact.csv).

If you can incorporate an audit export step and a dry-run for the eastern cluster, we can greenlight the window.

— Acme SRE
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Acme SRE <acme-sre@acmehealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet pinning & safety protocol — staging/rollback review

Thanks — capturing the changes and proposing concrete runbook steps below. I pulled the network layout and sketched the quarantine sequence (network-topology-v2.drawio).

Proposed runbook (short):
1) Preflight (T-72h): snapshot config, export audit logs to S3 (read-only bucket) and store sha256 digests; notify Acme compliance and share link.
2) Dry-run (T-24h): run pin on staging pool using canary flows; validate KV cache digest and latency.
3) Maintenance window: Sat 09/18 02:00-06:00 PT. Steps: cordon -> drain (control-plane first) -> pin runtime images -> verify health checks -> uncordon.
4) Rollback (trigger conditions): any of the criteria Marissa listed OR if post-pin latency P99 increases >200ms vs baseline for >5m. Rollback steps: automate unpin + rollback image to prior tag + purge KV partial state and rehydrate from snapshot.
5) Postmortem & audit (T+24h): collect logs, attach artifacts to the SF case.

I also recommend a small internal shiproom Tue 09/14 10:00 PT to rehearse rollback. I'll share the draw.io and the minimal checklist (see rollback_checklist.md).

Laura Bennett
Principal Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Acme SRE <acme-sre@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-06T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet pinning & safety protocol — staging/rollback review

All — thanks for the quick turnaround. Summary and next actions: 

- Acme: we'll add the audit export + sha256 digest step to Preflight and share the read-only S3 link to ops-legal@acmehealth.com.
- Marissa: please own the dry-run Tuesday rehearsal (09/14 10:00 PT). I'll send a calendar invite and a short shiproom agenda.
- Laura: please finalize the rollback playbook and add runbook snippets for the network affinity drain; attach the final draw.io link in the SF case.

Action items:
- [Soojin] Send S3 preflight export + digest to Acme compliance (by 2026-09-08 EOD).
- [Marissa] Dry-run execution plan + test matrix (by 2026-09-10).
- [Laura] Final rollback checklist + draw.io update (by 2026-09-09).

Related links: https://redwood.my.salesforce.com/0061A00000Xyz123, https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/staging-pin

Soojin
